assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear as values in an input column — not buried in output values or only mentioned in prose.
assertions.evidence:
At standard threshold, not above           | 30  | 650          | true              | REJECTED
At senior threshold (600)                  | 65  | 600          | true              | APPROVED

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '70', '650', 'APPROVED') — not abstract codes or raw booleans like 'true', '1'.
assertions.evidence: The 'Has Stable Income' column uses raw boolean values 'true' and 'false' (e.g., 'Standard approval | 30 | 700 | true | APPROVED'), which the assertion explicitly prohibits.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario                                   | Age | Credit Score | Has Stable Income | Status?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior at lower threshold', 'Missing income') — not outcomes ('Approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names include: 'Just above standard threshold', 'At standard threshold, not above', 'Below standard threshold regardless', 'Above threshold, no stable income', 'Age 65 qualifies for senior threshold', 'Missing income regardless of score', 'Senior - missing income' — all describing conditions, not outcomes.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Age', 'Credit score', 'Stable income', 'Decision?') — not code identifiers like 'customerAge', 'boolean'.
assertions.evidence: Column headers: Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Has Stable Income | Status?

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
